entities.summary: Claude François Bidal d'Asfeld, marquis d'Asfeld, was a French Marshal of France from 1700 to 1715, known for his leadership during the War of the Spanish Succession. Born on July 2, 1665, in Paris, Bidal d'Asfeld studied at the École Militaire and rose through the ranks, becoming a prominent figure in the French military. He played a key role in the Battle of Blenheim in 1704, where he distinguished himself for bravery. After the war, Bidal d'Asfeld continued to serve the French monarchy, participating in various campaigns and rising to the rank of Marshal. His military career was marked by several significant victories, including the Battle of Ramillies in 1706, where he led a French force to a decisive victory against the British and Dutch. Bidal d'Asfeld's military prowess and strategic thinking earned him recognition and respect from his peers and superiors. He died on March 7, 1743, and was buried in the Église de Saint-Louis in Paris. His legacy as a military leader and statesman has endured, with many historians considering him one of the greatest marshals of the 18th century.
